title: A live dashboard mirror for your other devices, a Standby mode you control, and site-wide fixes
teaser: If you run Taipo on more than one device, a Standby device can now show a live read-only mirror of your active device's dashboard instead of stale data — with a setting to turn that off if you'd rather keep full access everywhere. Plus clearer delete icons everywhere, and a fix for a Google connection error some of you hit.
body:
If you use Google Drive Backup across more than one device, a device that's currently in Standby now gets a small, automatically-refreshed snapshot of your Active device's Dashboard Home — so glancing at a secondary computer or a laptop shows real current numbers instead of whatever was there the last time that device actually ran something.

By default, a Standby device is also read-only elsewhere (Tasks, Collections, Add Tasks & Features, Edit Tasks, Settings, and Labs tools are locked until that device Takes Over) — new ground for Taipo, so we added a setting for it: Profile page → Automated Backups → "When this device is in Standby," choose Read-only (the new default) or Full Access, which keeps every device fully usable for browsing and editing like before, while still guaranteeing a Standby device's own scheduled tasks won't run there — only the Active device ever executes schedules, regardless of which mode you pick.

If you've seen a Google Drive Backup error mentioning "insufficient authentication scopes," we found and fixed the underlying cause and added clearer messaging (including showing exactly which permissions your connection currently has) so it's actually diagnosable instead of a cryptic failure. If backups or device status have been failing for you, reconnecting from the Profile page should resolve it now.

Site-wide: every delete icon across the app (Saved Results, Scheduled Tests, Collections, and more) is now a filled red circle instead of a plain grey glyph that was genuinely hard to see in either theme — also slightly bigger. Dashboard Home's Schedule card got a layout fix where Carousel Test rows could overlap their own countdown text.

For Labs users: Test Upper Carousel Order got a significant rework — Amazon shifted from reshuffling the carousel on every refresh to holding the same video set for a stretch before swapping all at once, so rapid single-page reloading stopped making sense. There's now a Round-Robin mode that cycles through a list of ASINs instead, plus a Media Kit tool for building a printable stats sheet to share with agents or sellers.

title: Action needed: reconnect Google once, plus a big Carousel Order Test upgrade
teaser: If you use Drive Backup or multi-device sync, please reconnect your Google account once after updating. Also: much smaller Carousel Order Test data, per-video highlight colors, product stats, and a new consistency column.
body:
⚠ If you use Google Drive Backup, device handoff, or multi-device sync: please reconnect your Google account once from the Profile page after this update. We switched to a more reliable connection method that keeps itself signed in correctly instead of quietly expiring every hour or so, but it means your existing connection needs to be re-established one time. Until you reconnect, scheduled backups and device status checks will fail (you'll see a warning on the Profile page) — a single click on Connect fixes it for good.

The Carousel Order Test tool (Labs) got a major upgrade. Saved test runs now take roughly 10x less space — a run now stores one summary row per unique video instead of one row per video per reload, with no loss to anything the Compare or Results screens actually show. Existing older runs aren't touched automatically, but you can select any of them and hit "Condense Selected" in Saved Results to shrink them too.

Other Carousel Test additions: highlighting multiple videos at once now gives each its own color instead of one shared color; a video's title now links straight to the video itself; product rating, price, how many were bought in the past month, and Best Seller Rank now show next to each tested product (cross-referenced from your own saved data, not a fresh lookup); a new "L Streaks" column shows the top 3 longest runs of consecutive reloads a video held the exact same rank (e.g. "17,17,10@R1") — separate from how often it showed up overall, and able to show whether Amazon keeps returning to a video for repeated long sittings or just parked it there once; and the Compare view now has summary cards (total unique videos/creators, most-shown video, date range, etc.) plus a "Copy AI Prompt" button tailored to spotting patterns across multiple saved runs.

We also fixed a real bug where duplicate blue "Amazon Session" tab groups could quietly pile up over weeks of normal use instead of staying at the one group they're meant to be.

title: Keep Video Info Updated, smarter video alerts, and a privacy note
teaser: A new task that keeps your video stats and status current, better Watcher Alerts for videos, and an anonymous usage ping we want you to know about.
body:
There's a new task you can add from Add Tasks & Features called "Keep Video Info Updated." Your existing CC-accepting task is built to be fast — it only ever looks at videos it hasn't seen before, which is right for finding new campaign opportunities but means a video's likes, views, and product tag stay frozen at whatever they were the first time it was discovered. This new task is the opposite: it re-checks every video you've already uploaded, once a day by default, so that data actually stays current. It also now tracks a video's real status (live, archived, etc.) — useful since Amazon recently started auto-publishing US videos to other marketplaces and archiving some originals in the process.

Watcher Alerts got several additions: new sample alerts for Views, Avg % Viewed, Avg View Duration, Last Edit Date, and Video Archived/Status Changed. Every alert now shows which of your saved tasks will actually produce the data it's watching, so you're not left wondering why an alert never fires. And if a video loses its tagged product, Taipo now remembers the original product's title and ASIN at the moment it happens — so "Video Lost Product Tag" alerts can actually tell you what to search Amazon for, instead of just saying a video lost its tag.

One more thing, in the interest of being upfront: this version adds an anonymous install ping, since the Chrome Web Store's own install count has looked frozen since launch. It sends a random install ID and your Taipo version — nothing about your Amazon account, earnings, or browsing. There's also an optional, off-by-default toggle in Settings ("Share anonymous usage stats") that, if you turn it on, additionally shares your task count and which built-in task types you use, to help us understand which features actually get used. See our privacy policy for the full details.

title: New Tutorials page, a more accurate Earnings graph, and a click-count fix
teaser: A new Tutorials page with walkthrough videos, a fixed Earnings graph default, a corrected click count, and a decluttered sidebar.
body:
There's a new Tutorials page in the sidebar with short walkthrough videos showing how to use Taipo — start with the general walkthrough, and let us know on the Feedback page if you'd like a video on something specific.

The Earnings graph on Dashboard Home now defaults to your most recent complete day instead of today — Amazon never finalizes same-day earnings, so showing today's still-incomplete number by default was misleading. You can still page forward to today manually any time.

We also found and fixed a bug that could double-count clicks in some cases, so your click totals are now accurate. Task-complete notifications and the Click Log card now also show how many clicks came in during that specific run, not just the running total.

The Carousel A/B Test tool's "View Saved Results" and "Compare Result Tables" screens are now merged into one — click any date to view it alone, or check several to compare them, with a new CSV export for a product's full saved history.

Finally, the left sidebar got a cleanup: a more compact clock, a two-column layout at the bottom, and tighter task cards, so it takes up less space and is easier to scan. Notifications now live next to the Edit Dashboard button up top, with an unread count badge.

title: Live Affiliate+ status on the upload page, plus a real bug fix
teaser: Click straight from the video-upload page to accept a product's Affiliate+ campaigns — checked live, not from a stale cache. Plus a real bug fix for silently-failed campaign accepts.
body:
Amazon's "Edit post" video-upload page now shows a live Affiliate+ status badge next to the product you've tagged: green if you're already in an active campaign, yellow if there's a new opportunity, grey if there's none. It's checked fresh against Amazon every time, not from Taipo's own cache, since a just-uploaded video's product has usually never been checked before.

Click the yellow badge to accept every available campaign for that product in one go, right from the upload page. Hovering over it shows how many opportunities are open, and flags how many look like they might already be claimed by other creators.

While building this we also found and fixed a real bug: Amazon's own "accept campaign" request can come back looking successful even when the campaign was actually rejected (for example, already fully claimed). Taipo now reads the real result instead of trusting that response — this fixes silent false-"accepted" reports anywhere Taipo accepts campaigns, not just the new upload-page badge.

A few smaller things shipped in this update too:
• Leftover "TAIPO" tab groups left behind by an interrupted run (for example, reloading the extension mid-task) now get cleaned up automatically.
• The Watchlist "Lists" picker got a visual refresh — the default list is checked automatically, and every change now shows a clear save confirmation.
• Comparison graphs on the Amazon Earnings Report can now be reordered by dragging them.
• YouTube video pages show the exact upload date next to the usual "x days ago" text, since that text isn't always precise.

Every new page-enhancement setting defaults to on but can be turned off anytime from Settings, or from the Amazon Page Enhancements wizard.

title: Welcome to Taipo
body:
Taipo automates the tedious parts of being an Amazon Associate or Influencer — pulling your clicks, orders, and earnings from Amazon, tracking Creator Connections campaigns, and running it all on a schedule so you don't have to check manually.

To get started: open Settings and enter your tracking IDs (Associates Base ID, Influencer Onsite ID, Storefront URL). Then head to Add Tasks & Features and set up your first task — ready-made cards for pulling earnings, tracking clicks, or auto-accepting Creator Connections campaigns. Each task can run on demand or on its own schedule, and everything it collects shows up on your Dashboard Home, which you can customize to show what matters most to you.

Questions or feedback? There's a Feedback page in the sidebar — we read every submission.
